nodes.title: Define shared site types
nodes.task: Define TypeScript interfaces and types: SiteMeta { title: string; description: string; locale?: string }, HeroAction { label: string; href: string; variant: 'primary' | 'secondary' }, HeroContent { eyebrow: string; title: string; subtitle: string; body: string; actions: HeroAction[]; visualLabel: string; visualTone: { from: string; to: string; accent: string } }, AuthorProfile { name: string; role: string; bio: string; location: string; avatarLabel: string; photoTone: { from: string; to: string; accent: string } }, ArticlePreview { id: string; title: string; excerpt: string; category: string; publishedAt: string; readTime: string; href: string; imageLabel: string; imageTone: { from: string; to: string; accent: string } }, TopicCategory { id: string; name: string; description: string; articleCount: number }, ContactChannel { label: string; href: string; kind: 'email' | 'github' | 'x' | 'linkedin' | 'rss' }, FooterLink { label: string; href: string }, SiteContent { meta: SiteMeta; hero: HeroContent; author: AuthorProfile; featuredArticles: ArticlePreview[]; categories: TopicCategory[]; contacts: ContactChannel[]; footerLinks: FooterLink[]; footerNote: string }. Export all symbols from output/types.ts.
nodes.acceptanceCriteria: output/types.ts exports SiteMeta, HeroAction, HeroContent, AuthorProfile, ArticlePreview, TopicCategory, ContactChannel, FooterLink, and SiteContent with the exact field shapes above. The file is type-only and compiles cleanly under strict TypeScript.

nodes.title: Inject Apple-like global styles
nodes.task: Implement injectGlobalStyles(): void and export appleUiClasses as a readonly object with semantic class names for page, shell, section, sectionHeading, grid, card, pill, buttonPrimary, buttonSecondary, mutedText, and divider. The injected stylesheet must define base typography, light background, spacing scale, rounded cards, soft shadows, hover transitions, responsive breakpoints, and reduced-motion behavior for the Apple-style visual system.
nodes.acceptanceCriteria: output/globalStyles.ts exports injectGlobalStyles() and appleUiClasses. Calling injectGlobalStyles() multiple times is idempotent and creates only one style tag. The exported class-name map is stable and usable by the UI components.

nodes.title: Seed static site content
nodes.task: Import SiteContent, HeroAction, and related types from output/types.ts. Export const siteContent: SiteContent with populated meta, hero, author, featuredArticles, categories, contacts, footerLinks, and footerNote. Use concise Apple-like copy, 3 to 6 featured articles, 4 to 6 categories, and gradient-friendly placeholder imageTone values; do not add any network fetches, CMS hooks, or runtime mutation.
nodes.acceptanceCriteria: output/siteContent.ts exports a fully populated siteContent object that conforms to SiteContent. All required arrays are non-empty, all URLs are static strings, and the module has no side effects.

nodes.title: Build the hero section
nodes.task: Implement HeroSection(props: { hero: HeroContent }): JSX.Element. Import HeroContent from output/types.ts and appleUiClasses from output/globalStyles.ts. Render the eyebrow, large headline, supporting subtitle, body copy, two CTA anchors from hero.actions, and a high-end abstract placeholder visual block using hero.visualTone and hero.visualLabel. Keep the component fully static, responsive, and free of local state.
nodes.acceptanceCriteria: output/HeroSection.tsx exports HeroSection with the exact prop shape above. The component renders all hero fields, renders both CTA actions, includes a placeholder visual area, and compiles without external data or state management.

nodes.title: Build author and contact section
nodes.task: Implement AboutSection(props: { profile: AuthorProfile; contacts: ContactChannel[] }): JSX.Element. Import AuthorProfile and ContactChannel from output/types.ts and appleUiClasses from output/globalStyles.ts. Render an author profile card with name, role, bio, location, avatar-style placeholder using profile.photoTone and profile.avatarLabel, plus a compact contact link list for the provided contacts.
nodes.acceptanceCriteria: output/AboutSection.tsx exports AboutSection with the exact prop shape above. The section renders the profile content and all provided contact links, uses no internal state, and compiles cleanly.

nodes.title: Build featured articles grid
nodes.task: Implement FeaturedArticlesSection(props: { articles: ArticlePreview[] }): JSX.Element and ArticleCard(props: { article: ArticlePreview }): JSX.Element. Import ArticlePreview from output/types.ts and appleUiClasses from output/globalStyles.ts. Render a responsive card grid with article category, title, excerpt, publishedAt, readTime, href, and a gradient placeholder image block derived from article.imageTone and article.imageLabel.
nodes.acceptanceCriteria: output/FeaturedArticlesSection.tsx exports FeaturedArticlesSection and ArticleCard with the exact prop shapes above. The grid renders one card per article, each card shows the required metadata, and the file compiles without fetching data or using complex interactions.

nodes.title: Build topic category section
nodes.task: Implement TopicsSection(props: { categories: TopicCategory[] }): JSX.Element and TopicPill(props: { category: TopicCategory }): JSX.Element. Import TopicCategory from output/types.ts and appleUiClasses from output/globalStyles.ts. Render a clean, responsive category grid or pill matrix showing name, description, and articleCount for each category.
nodes.acceptanceCriteria: output/TopicsSection.tsx exports TopicsSection and TopicPill with the exact prop shapes above. Each provided category is rendered, the layout is responsive, and the module contains no business logic beyond presentation.

nodes.title: Build the footer
nodes.task: Implement FooterSection(props: { footerLinks: FooterLink[]; footerNote: string }): JSX.Element. Import FooterLink from output/types.ts and appleUiClasses from output/globalStyles.ts. Render a minimal footer with link list, divider, and footerNote text using subdued Apple-style typography and spacing.
nodes.acceptanceCriteria: output/FooterSection.tsx exports FooterSection with the exact prop shape above. The footer renders all provided links and the footer note, uses the shared styling classes, and compiles without side effects.

nodes.title: Compose the page
nodes.task: Implement default function App(): JSX.Element. Import siteContent from output/siteContent.ts and import HeroSection, AboutSection, FeaturedArticlesSection, TopicsSection, and FooterSection from their respective files. Compose a single-page layout in the order HeroSection, AboutSection, FeaturedArticlesSection, TopicsSection, FooterSection, and optionally set document.title and meta description from siteContent.meta inside a harmless effect.
nodes.acceptanceCriteria: output/App.tsx default-exports App, renders the five showcase sections in the specified order, and uses siteContent as the only content source. The file compiles cleanly and contains no routing or backend logic.

nodes.title: Bootstrap the client app
nodes.task: Implement bootstrapApp(container: HTMLElement | null): void and invoke it against document.getElementById('root'). Import injectGlobalStyles from output/globalStyles.ts and App from output/App.tsx. Call injectGlobalStyles() once before rendering and mount App with React 18 createRoot; no-op safely if the container is missing.
nodes.acceptanceCriteria: output/main.tsx exports bootstrapApp and mounts App into the root element when present. Global styles are injected exactly once before first render, and missing root handling does not throw.

nodes.title: Add smoke test for core sections
nodes.task: Create a smoke test file that renders App with React Testing Library. Import App from output/App.tsx and siteContent from output/siteContent.ts. Assert that the hero title, author name, at least one featured article title, at least one category name, and at least one footer link are present in the document.
nodes.acceptanceCriteria: output/App.smoke.test.tsx passes under jsdom, verifies the presence of the main showcase sections, and does not rely on network or browser-only APIs outside the test environment.
